text:
kim (oncall): alert: apiserver 502s + etcd commit latency spike in eu-west-1. controller-manager leader election churning and several GPU onboarding pods Pending. noticed increased TCP retransmits on control-plane NICs after last-night kernel rollout. anyone on call? :eyes:

diego: i saw the kernel roll yesterday. we pushed 6.1.13 to control-plane to fix nvme resets. syslogs show repeated "TCP: Retransmission timeout" on the control-plane interfaces since the rollout. also load-balancer healthchecks showing intermittent failures.

anya: quick etcd status:
```
# kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd -o wide
etcd-ew1-0   1/1 Running   0   4h   10.2.1.5   eu-west-1a
etcd-ew1-1   0/1 CrashLoop  4   3h   10.2.2.6   eu-west-1b
```
leader logs show WAL fsync latency spikes and raft leader transfer attempts.

cloud-net: we see LB healthcheck RTT rising and a BGP flap that added an extra AS hop to storage path for a subset of AZs. combined with TCP retransmits that likely pushed the apiserver healthchecks over the short timeout window. increasing LB HC timeout should avoid false failovers.

infra-bot: alert: etcd_commit_latency > 400ms (eu-west-1) 7 ticket INC-8888 created.

diego: mitigation plan: (1) increase LB healthcheck timeout to 5s and add jitter, (2) roll back kernel on control-plane nodes to 6.1.12 where nvme fix not present, (3) reduce controller-manager concurrency to lower watch pressure. applying controller patch now:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment kube-controller-manager --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","args":["--concurrent-deployment-syncs=1","--concurrent-job-syncs=0"]}]}}}}'
```

harry: rolled back kernel on two control-plane nodes and reapplied tcp_congestion control/tuning (reduced tcp_retries2 and increased tcp_fin_timeout). LB healthcheck updated. early signal: apiserver 5xxs dropping and leader settled on same node for 8m. GPU Pending queue reduced ~35% after adding a small relaxed-taint GPU pool to accommodate immediate onboarding.

kim (oncall): good first pass. follow-ups: (1) hold kernel upgrades for control-plane until we validate nvme patch under our network profile, (2) add LB healthcheck backoff/jitter runbook, (3) implement gating for large onboarding jobs during control-plane maintenance windows, (4) evaluate exposing follower read endpoints for heavy watchers and add runbook step to reduce controller concurrency when etcd_commit_latency > 200ms. keeping incident open for 30m to confirm stability. :thumbsup:
